synthesis: ListScans/ListHits/ScanVehicleController gate the already-built ClickHouse query path on the string literals 'clickhouse:scans' / 'clickhouse:hits'. The only names Pennant ever defines are FeatureEnum::CLICKHOUSE_SCANS->slug() and CLICKHOUSE_HITS->slug(), which resolve (VERIFIED by execution) to 'clickhouse-scans' and 'clickhouse-hits'. Str::slug() cannot emit a colon, so the literals can never match a defined feature. Pennant's DatabaseDriver finds no stored row and no resolver, dispatches UnknownFeatureResolved, and returns false without persisting — so the ClickHouse path is reachable today only via session()->has('admin_impersonator'). Every Scans OCR search therefore runs the Postgres path, whose leading-wildcard ocr::text LIKE '%NA%' over an ~18-month window is unindexable and times out at 57014. Separately, HasRetryQuery::getTableRecords() logs to db-error and increments clarity.query_timeout unconditionally at the top of its catch block, BEFORE the retryUntil check, so every retry is counted as a distinct failure (measured 5.96x amplification). Outcome wanted: route Scans/Hits through the feature name that is actually defined, without changing the returned row set, and report one failure per search rather than one per retry.

Confirmed by executing App\Enums\FeatureEnum::CLICKHOUSE_SCANS->slug() in tinker. CLICKHOUSE_HITS->slug() === 'clickhouse-hits'.
ticket_corrections.why_it_matters: The ticket's conclusion (colon literal can never match) is CORRECT and unchanged. But the defect is a one-character typo — ':' where '-' belongs — not a wholly different naming scheme. It also changes what a prod `features`-table check should look for: rows named 'clickhouse-scans'/'clickhouse-hits' (the defined names) and 'clickhouse:scans'/'clickhouse:hits' (the checked names).

scope.summary: Hotfix, off deploy, SCOPED TO SCANS ONLY (narrowed 2026-09-17). questions.q: Rollout blast radius. After the fix, shouldUseClickhouse() becomes config('app.experimental.clickhouse.scans') && (isInsightLpr() || isProEnabled(CLICKHOUSE_SCANS)). The config is a single global boolean (true in this worktree's .env; prod value unverified). So the number of orgs that immediately start routing Scans searches onto ClickHouse equals the number of orgs holding the CLICKHOUSE_SCANS Pro override, plus all InsightLPR staff. The ticket's step 5 assumes a per-org enable for 2575 only. Which is it in prod: is CLICKHOUSE_SCANS an explicit per-org grant, or is it bundled into a Pro tier (in which case this lights up for every Pro org at once, against a 57.6 GiB CH ceiling that was already hit on 2026-09-11)? Also: does a features row literally named 'clickhouse:scans' or 'clickhouse-scans' already exist in prod?
questions.answer: No tier change (too risky). CLICKHOUSE_SCANS/HITS are not real Pro features - they are surfaced in no user-facing UI, and tests/TestCase.php:118 already excludes CLICKHOUSE_SCANS from makeOrgPro with the comment 'ClickHouse is opt-in'. ProTierEnum is the outlier. DECISION: remove the Pro/Pennant gating from the routing decision entirely; shouldUseClickhouse() checks config('app.experimental.clickhouse.scans') directly (plus the admin_impersonator escape hatch). All orgs then follow the same path, governed by one env var. ProTierEnum and the Feature::define lines are left untouched. Prod value of CLICKHOUSE_SCANS_ENABLED is being verified by Dalton (expected true).

questions.q: Scope of this ticket. Do you want all four code items in one PR (routing fix + kit-scoping parity + retry-log dedup + retryUntil), or just the routing fix and the log dedup now, with the row-set parity split out? The routing fix alone is 3 lines and stops the timeouts; the parity work is the part with a cross-repo dependency.

questions.q: is_visible parity. clarity.scans_cold has no is_visible column (only the raw CDC replica zod.public_scans does). The Postgres path filters is_visible = true via the ShowVisibleScan global scope, so the ClickHouse path would surface scans the Postgres path hides. Options: (a) accept and document the gap for now and open a chlocal ticket to carry is_visible into scans_cold; (b) hold the routing fix until chlocal lands the column. I would take (a) — the gap is pre-existing in the already-shipped CH path and affects only admin-impersonator sessions today, whereas the timeouts are live and daily. But this changes what customers see, so it is your call.
questions.answer: is_visible parity is OUT OF SCOPE for this ticket. It becomes a low-tier Jira follow-up for next sprint. The 5.36% gap (905,913 hidden of 16,916,753 scans over the last 2 days, measured read-only on prod) ships documented, for all orgs. Concern was raised explicitly and reaffirmed.

questions.q: Where the dedup guard lives. HasRetryQuery::$retryCount is a public Livewire property, so it does persist across the poll cycle within one component instance — meaning a public-property guard would dedupe retries. But that does not explain the ticket's measured 6 events per episode when retryUntil = 2 predicts 2 per search (2 searches = 4). The unexplained excess suggests either concurrent sessions or the component re-instantiating. Do you want (a) a component-property guard keyed on the filter hash (simple, dedupes the retry loop, which is the 5.96x -> ~2x win), or (b) a short-TTL cache key on user+filter hash (also dedupes across instances/sessions, closer to one-per-episode)? I would take (a) unless you already know the automation runs concurrent sessions.
questions.answer: Component-property guard keyed on a hash of the filter state (option a). Driver recommendation, stated twice, not overridden.
questions.source: ASSUMED:component-property guard keyed on filter hash

questions.q: retryUntil target value. Options: leave at 2, drop to 1 (one retry), or 0 (never retry a timed-out search). The ticket argues retrying an unindexable scan cannot succeed. Note HasRetryQuery is shared — it is also used by the Hits, MissedOpportunity and AffiliateStats list pages, so this is not a Scans-only change. I would take 1: keeps a single retry for a genuinely transient timeout on the other pages, and halves the load for this one.
questions.answer: retryUntil = 1. Keeps a single retry for a genuinely transient timeout on the other three pages that share HasRetryQuery, halves the load for this one. Driver recommendation, stated twice, not overridden.
